note: RIVERS: modelled floating macroplastic emitted to the sea each year at river mouths (tonnes per year, mid-point scenario), from Meijer et al. 2021, Science Advances (doi:10.1126/sciadv.aaz5803), data by The Ocean Cleanup on figshare, CC BY 4.0. This file keeps the 1500 largest of the 31819 outfalls in the source (729,412 of 1,005,984 t/yr); they are model estimates, not measurements, and the source has no river names. Row: [lat, lon, tonnes per year, river name (empty), ISO2 country of the nearest city, nearest city of 15,000+ people (GeoNames, CC BY 4.0), distance to that city in km]; the country is that of the nearest city and can be wrong close to a border. PEST: total pesticide use per hectare of cropland in kg/ha, [value, year], latest year per country (mostly 2023), FAO 'Pesticides Use' processed by Our World in Data, CC BY 4.0; national totals of active ingredients, partly estimated by FAO, saying nothing about which substances or where inside the country; a value of 0 is what the source reports and most likely reflects incomplete reporting, and very small countries with little cropland show extreme values; pestStats gives the median and 75th/90th percentiles across the 190 countries in this file. PESTBANNED: number of pesticide active ingredients or groups (out of 570 listed) recorded as banned in the country by the PAN International Consolidated List of Banned Pesticides, 7th Edition, Dec 2024 (copyright PAN International; only counts derived from it are stored here). PAN states the list is incomplete because many countries do not publish their bans, so a low or missing number means no information, not weak rules; it counts full bans only, not restrictions. The 27 European Union members share the EU-level count (plus national bans where listed); pestNotApproved (EU members and GB) counts listed substances not approved for use though not formally banned, and pestWithdrawn (US) those voluntarily withdrawn by industry. WATERGOOD: SDG indicator 6.3.2, percent of monitored water bodies with good ambient water quality, [value, year], years 2020-2023, UNEP via the UN SDG Global Database; reported by countries from very different numbers of monitored water bodies, so it is weakly comparable between countries. WASTEWATER: SDG indicator 6.3.1, percent of domestic wastewater flows safely treated, [value, year], years 2020-2024, WHO/UN-Habitat via the UN SDG Global Database; mostly estimates, domestic flows only (no industry or farm runoff). null means the source has no value for that country.
